item.title: GTA 6′s Map Contains Areas That Could Be Used In The ‘Future,’ Says Rockstar
item.summary: The studio also explained why you can't gamble in GTA 6 despite a casino being included on the map
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 features the largest open world Rockstar has ever created. It’s a map filled with locations to explore. However, after playing over 130 hours of GTA 6, there were still plenty of locations, including a zoo and a small northern town, that I never visited once during the story. And according to Rockstar, that’s because the map in GTA 6 was built for the “future.”
Ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6‘s launch, I asked Rockstar about the inclusion of at least two large casinos on the map. These locations can’t be entered and are never referenced or visited in the story or in any of the side missions I played. So I asked why Rockstar didn’t let Jason and Lucia bet it all on red.
“Jason and Lucia’s story didn’t feel like the right place for us to introduce gambling,” explained Rockstar VP of design Stephen Donkin. “Especially with the fine balance we sought throughout the economy.”
That’s fair. GTA 6 is the first Grand Theft Auto game to really make money feel important, and at times it can be hard to scrounge together enough cash to buy a new gun or fix up your car. So letting players save-scum their way to victory at the casino and have the characters come away with tens of thousands of dollars or more could have derailed the story Rockstar was trying to tell. But those casinos and other unused locations, like an extremely detailed zoo and a large graveyard, could end up being used for…something in the future.
“The map has been built for the long term and with many factors in mind,” said Donkin. “So there are a few areas on the map that give us options in the future should we have a gameplay or narrative need for them.”
Rockstar didn’t share any more details with me about what those “needs” could be, but it does seem that the company has built GTA 6 as something it can expand upon over time, possibly with expansions, updates, and/or some kind of online mode. For now, there’s plenty of GTA 6 for players to get lost in, and even those out-of-the-way locations are fun to explore.

item.title: GTA 6 Won’t Be Getting a Future Performance Mode, Even on PS5 Pro
item.summary: GTA 6 will be locked at 30 FPS on current consoles and won't get a future performance mode, even on PS5 Pro.
item.text:
In a rough turn of events for frame rate diehards, it seems Grand Theft Auto 6 won’t get a patch that boosts its frame rate at the expense of graphical fidelity. Speaking with Kotaku, Rockstar confirmed the game will not receive a performance mode on modern consoles, even on the beefier PlayStation 5 Pro.
Rockstar revealed earlier this month that GTA 6 targets 30 frames per second on all platforms, news that wasn’t well-received by a growing cohort of frame rate-conscious players. While many modern games offer options for console players to adjust a game’s visual fidelity — often with a quality mode that prioritizes visuals at the cost of frame rate, a performance mode that prioritizes frame rate (usually aiming for around 60 FPS), and a balanced mode that’s somewhere in between — GTA 6’s technical demands apparently make it difficult to run at higher frame rates on modern systems.
"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination," explained technology production director Marc Chambers. "On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."
What does this mean for a potential PC port?
While Rockstar hasn’t officially announced whether GTA 6 will eventually be released on PC, rumors suggest a port could arrive as early as 2027. That said, Chambers’ comments cast some doubt on this quick timeline, making it clear that the game is quite graphically intensive. A PC version would presumably let users toggle ray tracing and other visual features, which, based on Chambers’ comments, sound like something Rockstar is hesitant to allow. It's unclear how much of the studio's disinterest in a performance mode on console is related to the game's core technical infrastructure versus Rockstar's preference for how this experience is presented: it's possible they technically could ​​​​​​release a performance mode on console, but simply don't think the visual trade-off is worth it.
How have critics reacted to GTA 6’s frame rate?
Despite the hard frame rate cap, GTA 6 has received universal praise from critics, with a 99 score on Metacritic that makes it the highest-rated game of all time on that platform. Part of this praise comes from its impressive visual fidelity and detail, which apparently make Vice City feel authentic. Polygon’s review says that the 30 frame per second cap has "a negligible impact on the overall experience, given how smoothly it runs most of the time,” and that this is “a fair trade for a world that deserves its own line of postcards."
While the tech-focused YouTube channel Digital Foundry expressed some disappointment over the game’s 30 FPS cap, its testers added that GTA 6 is an interesting experiment in "seeing what was possible on this generation of consoles when settling for it." The review also described the title is "without a doubt the most visually striking game of this generation." Not a bad trade-off indeed.

item.title: 'We need to come together': On the eve of GTA 6, 1,600 Rockstar workers are voting on unionization
item.summary: "Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too."
item.text:
As I write this, reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6 have gone live. Gamers in New Zealand have been able to play it for almost six hours, and millions of people farther west are eagerly waiting for clocks to hit midnight in their own timezones. In preorder sales alone, GTA 6 has already generated over $1.6 billion in revenue, and will undoubtedly earn millions more over its launch weekend.
As Rockstar is poised to set historic records with its latest release, the workers who made it could be making history of its own: Over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on whether to form a union. If it wins recognition when the ballot closes on November 26, the Rockstar Games Workers Union would be the largest in the UK games sector, organizing workers at what's arguably the games industry's highest-profile studio—a major milestone in the push for unionization in game development.
In an op-ed for The Guardian, Rockstar animation programmer and union representative Nestor Uriarte said the studio's possible unionization is the product of a decade-long realization that "to tackle the industry's mounting challenges we need to come together." Union recognition, he said, would help safeguard the working conditions of the developers who built GTA 6 into an already record-breaking success.
"Behind these numbers are thousands of people whose talent and hard work make the games possible. With a recognized union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to," Uriarte said. "Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too."
Working conditions at Rockstar produced one of the early flashpoints in the advancing push for games industry unionization over recent years, sparked by employees' descriptions of its "death march" crunch culture and allegations of sexual assault. While the studio's taken steps towards a healthier workplace in the years since, employees have reported continuing concerns around gender pay gaps, crunch, and nebulous bonuses conditions.
Coinciding with the union vote, a Glasgow tribunal is weighing testimonies in the ongoing legal battle around Rockstar's alleged union-busting and firing of employees who had been involved in organization. Meanwhile, just days before a launch that's projected to earn landmark revenue, Rockstar parent company 2K reportedly laid off a third of the employees at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis.
"It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off," Uriarte said. "But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews
Union recognition, he said, would also provide developers with a greater ability to negotiate the rapid proliferation of AI in game development, which represents yet another threat of worker devaluation in an industry where one third of the labor force has been laid off in the last two years. A Rockstar union would help protect its workers' future—and the future of the studio.
"We’ve heard from colleagues who are nervous that the union is an outside troublemaking force that will threaten the company," Uriarte said. "But we’re not outsiders. We are hundreds of studio employees who live for Rockstar, its output, and the players. We want to see it succeed."

item.title: GTA 6 Withholds Your 100% Stats Until the End — For Good Reason
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 hides your 100% completion tasks until the very end, a move designed to keep players from getting overwhelmed.
item.text:
Completionists beware: Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to take you a very, very long time to complete. Rockstar Game’s open-world game is filled to the brim with things to do, see, and collect. You can go golfing, collect undersea treasures, find collectible trading cards, rack up medals at shooting ranges, scan landmarks, and so much more. Rockstar knows that it could get overwhelming fast, so GTA 6 was designed to combat that in one key way.
When playing through GTA 6, you’ll see a completion percentage on your save file. That number will only tick up when you complete story missions, a little less than 1% at a time. The rest of your collectible and activity progress is tracked in separate menus. However, you’ll also notice a locked menu option, with a line of text saying that it will open once you complete the story.
That’s your completionist menu. It shows you everything you need to achieve to get a true 100% save file, from finding all the special cars to sticking up every location you can. Once I unlocked it, the completion percentage on my save file kicked all the way down to 66%. After 10 hours of additional exploration, it had only ticked up another 2%. Needless to say, GTA 6 is not something you should expect to fully clear in a long weekend.
In an interview with Polygon ahead of the game’s release, Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson explained the decision to hide the completion menu until players got the story out of the way. Nelson said that it came down to not wanting to make players feel a compulsion to stop and do everything while playing. In fact, Nelson was insistent about fighting back against a lot of traditional open-world philosophies, saying that he took a “no checklists” approach to design. (Nelson admitted that he had to cede a little bit of ground and include a few checklists in the final game.) Notably, you won't unlock the ability to use cheats until rolling credits either. That further encourages you to explore in a normal way rather than cheating your way into tough end-game activities early.
It’s a small design consideration, but an important one. If you try to play GTA 6 like a normal open-world game, you’re bound to get lost in a sea of distractions. You’re constantly pulled into unexpected side quests, drawn towards roadside activities, or tempted into an easy robbery. But without a completion menu tracking your progression throughout the story, it’s easy to accept the fact that you probably can’t do it all at once. There’s no checklist to make you feel like you need to be robbing more banks or else you’re not doing enough.
Michael is the only one of the five who is already successful when you meet him, which makes him the only one whose real problem is boredom.
You picked the house first, and the rest of your life arranged itself around that one decision.
A bad family dinner is one you are paying for, while wondering how it ended up like this.
Ten years on you are trying to retire for the fourth time, and you will not manage it.
Franklin is the one who arrives wanting out, and everything he does is measured against whether it moves him closer to that.
You say nothing when somebody takes credit for your work, and you remember exactly who was in the room.
Money gets invested carefully in the thing that gets you out, which nobody else here would even consider.
People think this is as far as you are going. That is the single most useful thing they could believe.
Trevor is the least predictable character in the game and the most quoted, because he says out loud what everybody else is being careful about.
You introduce yourself to everyone, loudly, within an hour of arriving anywhere.
Money is gone by Thursday and you genuinely could not tell anybody where it went.
People think you do not know exactly what you are doing. You do, and that is the unsettling part.
Lester is the one who sees the whole board, and he is written as the opposite of everybody around him: no volume, no impulse, all preparation.
Yo

item.title: GTA 6 Finally Changed The Default Rockstar-Game Controls
item.summary: If you've played Rockstar series like Grand Theft Auto or Read Dead Redemption over the past few decades, then you're familiar with their default control scheme, which maps sprinting to a face button instead of the left analog stick. But Grand Theft Auto VI isn't being hailed as a revolutionary game for nothing--at long last, the default scheme has changed. As we learned while playing Grand Theft Auto VI, instead of the default setup mapping sprint to a button (A on Xbox and X on PS5), the game maps it to the left analog stick. However, you're free to switch it back to the style used in games like Red Dead Redemption 2, if you prefer. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAhUXOYNuH4 This is a very handy change, because mapping sprinting to a face button effectively stops you from being able to easily do some of your other actions, unless you have no dignity like me and will use your own face to press a button when your hands are full. The new default control scheme is far from the most impressive thing in Grand Theft Auto 6, of course. The game earned a rare 10/10 in our GTA 6 review , with Tamoor Hussain calling it "the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach." For more on the game, check out our ever-expanding GTA 6 guides hub and learn what you should do first . That shouldn't include buying a whole new pro controller , however.

item.title: GTA 6 Launches With a 99 on Metacritic, Tying the Highest-Rated Game Ever
item.summary: GTA 6 has a 99 Metacritic score from 100 critic reviews, tying the highest score ever and beating every previous GTA game.
item.text:
Thirteen years of waiting ended with a number only one other game has ever reached and even that game's previous record comes with a caveat. Grand Theft Auto VI is sitting at a Metacritic score of 99, built from 100 critic reviews with not a single mixed or negative verdict among them. For Rockstar Games, a studio whose titles already live in the mid-to-high 90s, this is new ground.
A 99 ties the highest Metascore ever recorded, a mark held until now only by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time from 1998. GTA VI is still not on uncharted territory but it matches the previous record with roughly four times the review count and a clean sweep of positive scores, where Ocarina's 99 rested on a far smaller sample. It also clears the series' own ceiling, topping Grand Theft Auto IV's 98 and the 97s that Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto III have carried for years.
The all-time Metacritic high, and where GTA 6 sits
GTA 6 ties the record and tops every Grand Theft Auto before it.
The scores behind that average are about as lopsided as review day gets. On Metacritic's listing the perfect marks stack up fast, with IGN handing out a 10 and calling it "the single most impressive video game I've ever played," Game Informer's Matt Miller scoring it a 10, and Windows Central's Jez Corden writing that it is "quite possibly a contender for best game ever" after asking his team if he could somehow file an 11 out of 10. Kotaku landed on "a masterpiece of open-world design," in its review. Those are the writers' verdicts rather than ours, but the consistency across a hundred of them is the story.
Nearly every review points at the same thing. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos' relationship is the piece critics keep calling the heart of the game, the element that lifts it past earlier entries. Game Informer described their dynamic as "video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance," Edge cast the duo as a partnership "driven forward not by fear, but by love," and Kotaku said they "feel like a real couple" worth rooting for. It is the grounded, character-first direction Rockstar carried over from Red Dead Redemption 2,and the critics treated it as the payoff.
The acclaim is not completely edgeless, and we would not pretend otherwise. The recurring caveat across reviews is the locked 30fps on current hardware, including the PlayStation 5 Pro, which Digital Foundry traced to a CPU limit rather than a choice Rockstar can just patch away easily. A handful of writers also noted occasional control friction or a late pacing dip. Finally, the Metacritic user score is still pending, with early fake ratings scrubbed and the critic figure can still change as more reviews come in.
This is the validation every thread of our coverage pointed toward. It is the game that already led the Game Awards with eight nominations, the one Rockstar delayed twice for polish after a decade of building the world and the density the Game Informer cover first laid out. Take-Two Interactive had it on track for the biggest launch in history on the commercial side and now the critical side is matching the hype with the highest number a game has ever posted.
The sales were never the question. A 99 from 100 reviews with no negatives is the part nobody could guarantee and it puts GTA VI among the best-reviewed games ever made.
Rockstar did not just clear the bar it set with Grand Theft Auto V with the newest Grand Theft Auto. It tied the highest one the medium has even though it didn't even need to be this good.
Does GTA 6 deserve to tie the highest-rated game of all time, or is some of that 99 the weight of 13 years of hype talking?

item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is shaping up to be a monumental release. From its gripping narrative to the sprawling open world of Leonida, there’s seemingly no shortage of content to sink your teeth into. If you’re planning to spend countless hours exploring everything the game has to offer, you’ll likely have a lengthy trophy hunt ahead of you, too.
With collectibles to discover, activities to complete, and a story to finish, GTA 6 could be a completionist’s dream—or a nightmare, depending on how you look at it. Earning the coveted Platinum Trophy is likely to require plenty of dedication, especially if you’re aiming to achieve 100% completion.
Be warned, though: this guide contains major GTA 6 spoilers. The trophy list includes several hidden achievements tied directly to the game’s narrative, meaning you could accidentally stumble upon some significant story details if you’re not careful. If you’d rather experience Leonida without knowing what lies ahead, we’d strongly recommend avoiding the hidden trophy section.
If you’re willing to risk a few spoilers, here’s everything you need to know about the GTA 6 trophy list. And if you haven’t purchased GTA 6 yet, you can buy it here.
How Many Achievements & Trophies In Grand Theft Auto 6?
There are 55 trophies and achievements to earn in Grand Theft Auto 6 across PlayStation and Xbox.
That’s slightly more than both Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, making GTA 6’s trophy list a potentially hefty undertaking for completionists. Of course, GTA 5 eventually received additional trophies through its GTA Online updates, so there’s every chance GTA 6 could follow a similar path after launch.

item.title: GTA 6 Just Set a Streaming Record With Over 6 Million Peak Viewers at Launch
item.summary: StreamsCharts puts GTA VI's preliminary streaming launch peak at 6.38 million concurrent viewers, versus the previous 1.74 million record.
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI broke a record before most of the world could even press start. As the first regions came online, particularly the uber proud New Zealand, millions flooded onto Twitch, YouTube and Kick to watch the lucky few playing GTA VI and the live-streaming analytics firm StreamsCharts says Rockstar Games just posted the biggest streaming launch the medium has seen and it's not even close.
The numbers moved fast and they're still growing as we speak. StreamsCharts first clocked a peak above 5.3 million concurrent viewers a few minutes into the game's release then updated to a preliminary 6.38 million a few hours later, with the count still rising as GTA VI unlocked for the rest of the world.
For scale, that blows past the previous benchmark, Valorant's closed beta, which drew around 1.74 million back in 2020. It also tops GTA VI's own gameplay reveal, the Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look that pulled roughly 3.97 million concurrent viewers in August and became Netflix's most-watched title of its week.
The spread across platforms is its own story, laid out in StreamsCharts' launch report. All of this is preliminary analytics data rather than an official Rockstar figure and it counts people watching, not playing or buying.
StreamsCharts' combined figure sits at a preliminary 6.38 million and counting.
GTA VI is console-only with no PC version at launch, which may help explain why some viewers are watching rather than playing. Thirteen years of waiting met a release window marked by a viewership peak no game has come close to.
It is one more record in a launch snapping them off by the hour. The same game just tied the highest Metacritic score ever recorded and it also broke European internet-traffic records before it even launched after already being on track for the biggest launch in history on the commercial side, with a 24-hour creator livestream feeding the stream counts further.
Off-screen or on, the game is rewriting the record book.
The streaming peak could climb as the United States and the rest of the map hit midnight, so the final figure is not even set. The point is that it was never a contest. Viewers are tuning in to GTA VI at a scale the industry has never recorded for a game launch.
Were you one of the millions watching GTA 6 streams before you could play, or holding out to go into Leonida completely blind?

Six million people watching a game most of them cannot even play yet is the most GTA VI stat of all.

item.title: Rockstar Drops GTA 6 Festival Set Times With Cactus Jack Finale
item.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 Miami festival schedule puts Metro Boomin at midnight and the Cactus Jack finale at 12:40 a.m. local time.
item.text:
The launch party now has a running order and it's a doozy. Rockstar Games has published the full set times for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, the one-off Miami concert it is throwing to mark the game's arrival.
The Grand Theft Auto VI show runs November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami, with doors opening at 4:00 p.m. local time and the festival itself pushing into the early hours of the morning. It is a 17-and-over event with no on-site parking and two stages running back to back all night. The event is presented alongside PlayStation and produced by the team behind Miami's III Points. The on-site Store at Mana Wynwood will be stocked with special GTA VI gear for anyone who got in.
Unfortunately, tickets were never a walk-up affair, handed out through a DICE lottery that closed on November 10 at two per code. Tough luck, if you didn't get one.
Rockstar laid out the schedule on its official account, with the event page and the November 9 Newswire announcement carrying the rest of the detail. Stage One builds toward a Cactus Jack finale from Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black and Sofaygo that doesn't start until 12:40 a.m., while Stage Two hands its midnight slot to Metro Boomin. Cardi B, a Justice DJ set and a Rauw & Friends set with Tainy fill out the headline run.
How GTA 6: The Festival plays out across both stages
et times per Rockstar's official graphic and subject to change on the night.
Every act is pulled from the game's own sound, the in-game radio stations, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album and the original score Justice composed for the game. It is the same crossover of real-world music and GTA VI that runs through our live soundtrack tracker, down to the "Flower in a Hurricane" single that scored the launch trailer.
According to Rockstar, every dollar from ticket sales goes to local Miami charities as a thank-you to the city, with a follow-up post naming nine recipients including The Miami Foundation, Miami Bethany Community Services, Hermanos de la Calle, Live Healthy Little Havana and Coconut Grove Crisis Food Pantry, alongside funds for the city's firefighters and police associations.
The Festival is the capstone on a takeover that has swallowed the whole city. Miami-Dade already committed $3.9 million to turn itself into Vice City for the launch, a real club became the in-game NINE1NINE for a launch party, the developers funded over 7,000 free tickets for a Haitian music event in the real Little Haiti, the Miami Heat turned a home game into a Vice City night and the giant sign on the Kaseya Center has been up for weeks. The Festival is where all of that comes together in one room.
Two days after the game unlocks for everyone, the city that spent a year becoming Vice City gets to throw the after-party for it. Bringing Travis Scott, Metro Boomin and Justice together for a Miami charity night is a launch-party flex that fits GTA's outsized profile.
If you snagged a wristband, are you planting yourself at Stage One for the Cactus Jack closer, or bouncing between stages to catch Metro Boomin and Justice back to back?

item.title: How GTA 6 Cheats Work and Why You Have to Finish the Whole Story First
item.summary: All 61 cheats in GTA 6 stay unusable until you finish all 91 main story missions, even if you tackle unlock challenges earlier.
item.text:
Cheats are part of what made Grand Theft Auto a cultural icon, the tank codes and infinite ammo tricks passed around schoolyards for 25 years. Grand Theft Auto VI is no different but Rockstar Games has put them further out of reach than it ever has and we have no choice but to fill up our GTA VI cheats page slowly because of it.
If you've heard rumours that you cannot use a cheat in GTA VI until you have beaten the game, it's true. The game has 61 cheats covering player effects, combat, vehicle spawns, environment tweaks and screen filters. None of them are available from the jump. Instead, GTA 6's dedicated Cheats section only appears in the Progress Menu once you have cleared all 91 main story missions across Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos' campaign. You can chip away at the individual unlock challenges mid-playthrough, winning shooting-range medals, clearing activities or shaking wanted levels, but the codes stay dead until the credits roll.
You can't brute force your way out of this. The menu itself refuses to show up before the story is done. We know. We've tested. The catch after that is the price of using one. Turning on cheats disables saving and blocks trophies and achievements for the rest of that session, so you can't keep the progress of anything you do with a code active.
The change is stark when compared to Grand Theft Auto V, where button and phone codes worked in free roam within your first hour in Los Santos. A handful of vehicle spawns in that game, the Duke O'Death, the Dodo and the Kraken, needed specific unlocks, but the system itself was open from the start and turning a cheat on only switched off achievements while still letting you save. Grand Theft Auto IV, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto III all let you cause chaos long before the ending. No earlier entry gated the whole cheat menu and the act of using it, behind full story completion.
The design tracks with a studio that built this game to make you play it straight, holding its biggest toys back until the story has settled its weight. Cheats become a reward for finishing rather than a shortcut that can hollow out a first playthrough, a defensible call even though it stings the players who treat a fresh GTA as a sandbox from minute one.
Either way, the decision, as we've already mentioned, shapes how we are covering this. Our GTA VI cheats page is live and it will grow as we unlock each code ourselves rather than by copying a day-one list scraped from everyone else.
We'd rather take the long way, verify every cheat and its unlock challenge in our own game and update the page as we go. The cheats are a post-game prize this time, so earning the right to document them properly is the whole point.
Do you want cheats as a post-game reward you have to earn, or should a new GTA hand you the tank code the second you hit free roam like it always used to?

I cannot decide if it is genius or if it misses the point of cheats entirely. Half the fun of a new Grand Theft Auto used to be breaking it in hour one.
